title: Pathophysiology Of Animal Disease
description: Pathophysiology of animal disease is presented, using an "organ systems" approach. Students learn mechanisms of response to disease of common domestic animals. Includes study of the common diseases of domestic animals with emphasis on the dog and cat. Emphasis is on learning how patients respond to disease and how the effective veterinary technician assesses and intervenes to benefit the patient. Topics include: etiology, pathogenesis, clinical signs, diagnostics, and nursing management of selected diseases. Principles of vaccination, disease prevention, public health, client education, and zoonosis. Students will build on their personal knowledge as well as information that they've learned in previous courses. Intended for students in the Veterinary Technology Program; enrollment is limited to students accepted in the program.
outcomes: Using multiple peer-reviewed sources in the library database, research an approved disease of interest. Create a handout using simplified language geared toward client education that discusses common signalment, etiology, pathophysiology, treatment, monitoring and prognosis of the disease.

Using multiple peer-reviewed sources in the library database, research an assigned disease and, using appropriate medical terminology, create a presentation for veterinary technician peers that describes the etiology, pathophysiology, diagnosis, differential diagnoses, and prognosis of the disease.
objectives: Describe physiology of the immune system and immune functions within specific organ systems.
Explain how vaccinations protect animals from disease.
Explain the role of veterinary technicians in the compassionate nursing care of patients.
Explain the etiology, pathogenesis, clinical signs, diagnostics, treatment, nursing assessments, and clinical management of selected diseases organized by body systems.

Describe select infectious and parasitic diseases of domestic animals, including etiology, mode of transmission, natural history or life cycle, pathogenesis, clinical signs, diagnostic procedures, and clinical nursing management.
Explain the role of the veterinary technician in "One Health."
Create a plan for learning about disease and the role of the veterinary nurse.
content: Review of immune system and immune functions
Normal anatomy and physiology in wellness
Stressors: causes of cellular adaptation, injury, and death
Veterinary technicians and compassionate nursing care of patients
Selected diseases organized by body systems
Cardiovascular, respiratory, integument, gastrointestinal, renal, endocrine, musculoskeletal, neurologic, and reproductive systems
Infectious and parasitic diseases of domestic animals
Veterinary technician's role in public health and zoonoses
Discussion of USDA (US Department of Agriculture) reportable diseases
Create a plan for learning about disease and the role of the veterinary nurse
Orientation to the professional periodical literature
Use of reference materials and databases
